attribution.note: Marcus's own footnote text in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: There are two parts. The firm part: the product names make customers think the cars are far more capable than they are. The consequence part (inattention, accidents, deaths) sits under 'may', so it is hedged and not scored. Only the firm naming-to-belief part is scored.

contract.note: Reading the names as Autopilot and FSD fits the context and is fair. The contract also scores the hedged 'may' pathway; under policy that part should not be scored. The firm part can be judged on the contract's plain reading.

evidence.note: IIHS comparative survey: names shown without brands, and Autopilot drew more unsafe beliefs. It directly tests the naming-to-belief link, though it measures stated beliefs and covers only Autopilot.
Regulator decision finding that 'Autopilot' marketing from 2021 on was misleading about capability. This covers the period of the claim. Published before the evaluation date.
NTSB found overreliance and distraction in a fatal crash. That bears on the hedged pathway, which is not scored, and the report does not tie the driver's beliefs to the name.
IIHS 2022 owner survey says the Autopilot name implies more capability than the system has, but notes demographic and design confounds. Super Cruise users misused their system more.

reviews.rationale: The firm claim that the names lead customers to overestimate capability is backed by an IIHS comparative naming study and California DMV's finding that the 'Autopilot' marketing was misleading. The confounds IIHS raised in 2022 limit how much is attributable to the names but do not refute the link. The consequences framed with 'may' are not scored.

semantics.note: 'We shouldn't expect' is advice about what to expect, but it amounts to an unhedged forecast that Level 5 won't arrive soon. The scope (any point A to B, safely) and the vague horizon are preserved.

contract.note: The contract correctly notes there is no fixed endpoint and that continued non-arrival cannot settle the forecast. The result depends on how 'any time soon' is read.

evidence.note: October 2026 interview saying Level 5 does not exist yet. That fits non-arrival so far, but it is one expert's view, not a deployment census, and gives no endpoint.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows no verified Level 5 deployment as of October 2026, so nothing contradicts the forecast. But 'any time soon' has no deadline, and under the contract's early-resolution rule non-arrival cannot conclusively settle a negative forecast. Unresolved.

semantics.note: The antecedent ('without it', meaning no outlier solution) is preserved. 'Remain a pipe dream' is fairly rendered as 'will not be achieved'. No horizon was stated.

contract.note: The contract rightly flags that the antecedent has no independent test and risks being circular. Its status is unknown.

evidence.note: July 2026 IIHS says Level 5 does not yet exist. That is no counterexample, but it neither establishes the antecedent nor proves the claimed necessity.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. No evidence independently establishes whether the outlier problem has been solved, so the antecedent's status is unknown, and the claim is not scored. That Level 5 has not been achieved settles neither the antecedent nor the necessity claim.

semantics.note: Present-tense observation that Level 5 capability did not exist as of the post. Faithful.

contract.note: The ordinary reading of Level 5 as unrestricted capability, and the June 2022 target period, are fair.

evidence.note: Verge report from the post date states there were no Level 5 vehicles. This is reputable contemporaneous reporting on the industry-wide status.
June 2022 CPUC permit for Cruise. It is labelled a company disclosure but is a regulator release. It shows driverless service limited to set streets, hours, speeds and weather, so not Level 5.

reviews.rationale: Reporting from the post date says no Level 5 vehicles existed. The most advanced driverless permit then (Cruise in San Francisco) was tightly restricted. Nothing in the packet shows unrestricted Level 5 capability by June 15, 2022.
